ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(eo1): give the slow Qwen2.5-VL image processor CPU images (#5146)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(eo1): give the slow Qwen2.5-VL image processor CPU images (#5146)

lerobot-rollout, lerobot-train, and the predict_action and
build_inference_frame helpers move the batch to the policy device before
the preprocessor runs. EO-1's Qwen step then passed GPU image tensors to
the default (slow) Qwen2.5-VL image processor, which reads pixels with
NumPy and fails:

    TypeError: can't convert cuda:0 device type tensor to numpy.

lerobot-eval fails the same way with IsaacLab Arena environments, which
return camera images on the GPU. Other environments and the policy
server pass CPU images.

Move the images to the CPU in the Qwen step when the slow processor is
used. The move uses move_state_dict_to_device, which builds new message
containers, so the transition the previous step returned keeps its GPU
images. The fast processor (use_fast_processor=True) already handles GPU
tensors, so its images stay on their device, as before. The preprocessor's
last step still moves its outputs to the policy device, and CPU input is
unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Haoming Song <haomingsong24@gmail.com>

ns0:entry.ns0:title: chore(dependencies): allow filelock 4.x, require 4.2.1 or newer (#5154)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
chore(dependencies): allow filelock 4.x, require 4.2.1 or newer (#5154)

LeRobot pins filelock below 4.0, which keeps it on releases affected by
GHSA-69hj-f68j-2879: on Unix, FileLock empties (and with an explicit
mode, re-permissions) any file another local user renames or hard-links
onto the lock path. LeRobot's sidecar cache uses FileLock, and
huggingface_hub's WeakFileLock passes mode=0o664. The fix is in 4.2.1,
along with several other advisories, and no 3.x release has it.

This change raises the pin to `filelock>=4.2.1,<5.0.0` and updates
uv.lock. The only package that moves in the lock is filelock itself,
from 3.32.7 to 4.2.4.

LeRobot uses filelock in a small way: `FileLock(path, timeout=...)` as a
context manager and `Timeout` in the streaming sidecar code, plus
huggingface_hub's `WeakFileLock` for dataset metadata. 4.1.0 rejects a
bool or string timeout; LeRobot passes only numbers. The 4.0 breaking
change is limited to `SoftReadWriteLock`, which LeRobot does not use.

Tested on Linux x86_64 with Python 3.12, in two fresh environments built
from the old and the new uv.lock (they differ only in filelock):

- tests/test_streaming_sidecar.py, tests/datasets/test_dataset_metadata.py
  and the other streaming and sidecar tests (20 files, 431 tests):
  all pass on both filelock 3.32.7 and 4.2.4.
- A small two-process check that `FileLock` and `WeakFileLock` raise
  `Timeout` while another process holds the lock, and acquire once it is
  released: same result on both versions.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(xvla): compute select_action chunks through predict_action_chunk …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(xvla): compute select_action chunks through predict_action_chunk (#4827)

* fix(xvla): compute select_action chunks through predict_action_chunk

lerobot-rollout --use_torch_compile compiles a policy by wrapping its
predict_action_chunk with torch.compile. X-VLA's select_action called the
internal _get_action_chunk instead, so the compiled wrapper never ran and
X-VLA stayed uncompiled, while the rollout still logged that compilation
was configured. X-VLA has no compile setting of its own, so this wrapper
is the only way the flag can reach it.

Compute each new chunk through predict_action_chunk, as most chunking
policies already do, and pass the noise argument on to it.
predict_action_chunk calls the same _get_action_chunk. Its observation
queue update now runs only on the ticks that compute a chunk, which
changes nothing for X-VLA because its only queue holds actions.

The new test keeps the real predict_action_chunk and records each call to
it, the same way the rollout installs its wrapper, and replaces only the
chunk computation inside it with a fresh random chunk per call. It checks
that select_action computes exactly two chunks through predict_action_chunk,
passes the same batch and noise each time, and returns the first
n_action_steps actions of the first chunk and then the first action of the
next one. It fails without the change.

* test(xvla): drop select_action routing test
